task_instruction: Suggest meeting at the local school after a community event, include compensation and map printed.
task_details: Write to elder named Ljubica in selo Ravnica asking to meet at the school after the weekend community event to discuss communal land points. Specify duration (about 30–45 minutes), meeting place school (centre of selo), say you'll bring printed map and offer 1,500 RSD or a small gift, and offer flexibility if they cannot stay after the event.
personalized:
Dear Ljubica,

Greetings. I will be in Ravnica this Saturday for the community event and would like to speak with you about communal land markers and shared grazing areas. If you have time after the event, could we meet at the school (centre of selo) for about 30–45 minutes? I will bring a printed map.

I can offer 1,500 RSD or a small gift in thanks. If it is not possible to meet after the event, please tell me another time that suits you.

Thank you — I appreciate your time.

Marko Petrović
(If helpful, I can show how this will help municipal planning.)

task_instruction: Request a short interview by phone or in person, offering evening or weekend in-person options and reimbursement.
task_details: Email elder named Vera in selo Bukovac offering a choice of a quick phone call (10–15 minutes) or an in-person visit (30–45 minutes) at the village centre. Provide meeting place, mention bringing a printed map and GPS, state small cash compensation (1,000 RSD) for in-person, and ask which option they prefer.
personalized:
Dear Vera,

Greetings. I am updating the map of Bukovac and would like to ask a few questions about public wells and the old trail. If it is easier for you, we can do a short phone call (10–15 minutes). If you prefer meeting in person, I can come to the village centre for about 30–45 minutes on an evening or weekend.

I will bring a printed map and GPS. For an in-person meeting I can offer 1,000 RSD. Please tell me which option you prefer and what time suits you.

Thank you — I appreciate your time.

Marko Petrović
(If you want, I can call first to agree a time.)

task_instruction: Invite elder to a morning meeting including permission to note names of informants and village features.
task_details: Write to elder named Rade in selo Velika Poljana requesting a morning meeting at the central well to discuss names of fields, meadows and family plots. Mention duration about 30–45 minutes, printed map provided, request permission to note names and features, offer 1,500 RSD, and provide alternative date options.
personalized:
Dear Rade,

Greetings. I am recording traditional names for fields, meadows and family plots in Velika Poljana and would be grateful for your help. Could we meet by the central well on Tuesday morning at 09:00 for about 30–45 minutes? I will bring a printed map.

May I note the names you give and the locations? I will only use them for the map and community record. I can offer 1,500 RSD for your time. If that morning does not suit, please suggest another day.

Thank you — I appreciate your time.

Marko Petrović

Marko Petrović

Before we agree on storage, could you confirm whether you need me to increase insurance or add the building as an interested party? Regards,
Marko

I’d like permission to keep one mapping drone and two Li-po batteries in a small locker on the third floor. Best,
Marko

Best regards,
Marko

Hello Viktor,

I’m asking for permission to store three Li-po battery packs in a lockable box in the equipment room under these conditions: batteries will be stored at roughly 40–60% SOC, checked monthly and logged, never charged on site, and Li-po batteries stored in approved container inside the box. I will follow manufacturer storage guidelines and keep the area clearly labelled.

My liability insurance is (policy ref: RS-LOG-4432). I can maintain a simple log (date, SOC, condition) and share it with you on request. I’m happy to sign an agreement describing these procedures.

Regards,
Marko

Mention you will follow manufacturer storage guidelines and Li-po batteries stored in approved container, provide insurance ref and indicate willingness to adjust storage plan per building rules.
personalized:
Hello Siniša,

Quick question: are there any building restrictions about storing small UAVs or Li-po batteries on the premises? I will follow manufacturer storage guidelines and Li-po batteries stored in approved container, but I want to make sure we meet building rules.

I have liability insurance (policy ref: RS-ASK-5522) and will adjust the storage plan to match any restrictions you point out. If allowed, I’ll propose a storage location and agreement for your review.

Best,
Marko

If you approve storage of my drone batteries in the equipment locker, I will attach a laminated emergency procedure next to the locker with immediate steps (isolate, evacuate if needed, call emergency services), my contact numbers and my insurance policy ref (policy ref: RS-EMG-7104). Regards,
Marko

Dear Ana,

During mapping campaigns I sometimes need to bring extra batteries (up to five Li-po packs) for back-to-back flights. May I store them in the lockable equipment room for the campaign duration (typically 2–3 days)? I will follow manufacturer storage guidelines and Li-po batteries stored in approved container and will not charge any batteries on site. I will give you advance notice before each campaign.

My liability insurance is (policy ref: RS-CAM-1447). If you approve, I will document dates and return items immediately after the campaign.

Thanks,
Marko

Hello Dubravka,

For both safety and security, may I store my drone and Li-po batteries in the equipment locker? I will follow manufacturer storage guidelines and Li-po batteries stored in approved container. As an added security measure I’m willing to install a small camera outside the locker (recording only) so we have a log of access. I will cover installation costs and address any privacy concerns you raise.

My liability insurance policy ref is RS-CAM-4477. I’ll sign an agreement describing the camera and data retention period if you approve.

Best,
Marko

Thank you,
Marko

I request permission to store several Li-po battery packs for operational needs with the condition that I will rotate stock so no battery sits in storage for longer than three months. Regards,
Marko

personalized: Hey — you in for Sat? Meet 08:30 at the central bus station. Can you check the Saturday morning bus from your place and tell me if you'll come by bus or by car? Hike's 10 km with a few steep sections, so plan accordingly. See you — can't wait.

persona.name: Marko Petrović
persona.demographics: Belgrade, Serbia; Serbian; raised in a small village near Niš, has lived and worked across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro and Croatia
persona.profession: Senior GIS Analyst & Cartographer — Village-scale mapping and spatial data analyst
persona.education: MSc in Geomatics (University of Belgrade); BSc in Geography; Esri ArcGIS Professional Certification; Certified QGIS trainer; UAV/drone mapping course
persona.brief_background: Marko blends time in the field with long evenings at his workstation, stitching together satellite imagery, drone captures and interviews with elders to produce detailed village maps. He submits edits to OpenStreetMap, trains local volunteers to collect GPS points and writes small scripts to automate data cleaning. He looks for patterns in settlement changes and infrastructure gaps so NGOs and municipal planners can make practical decisions.
persona.interests_lifestyle: drone piloting and aerial photography, OpenStreetMap contributions, hiking and field surveys in rural areas, Balkan folk music and village festivals, Python and R scripting for spatial analysis, map design and cartographic aesthetics, weekend camping with a field GPS, mentoring university students

general_writing_style.tone: Professional and pragmatic with a quietly warm, mentoring undercurrent. Prefers clear, actionable communication — answers questions directly, flags uncertainties, and defers to local knowledge when relevant. Slightly informal with colleagues and volunteers, more formal with institutional partners or written deliverables.
general_writing_style.syntax: Predominantly short to medium-length declarative and imperative sentences for instructions and reports, with occasional longer complex sentences when explaining methodology or interpreting spatial patterns. Often structures technical notes as stepwise numbered instructions or compact paragraphs with parenthetical clarifications (e.g., coordinates, CRS codes). Rarely uses ornate language; prioritizes clarity and reproducibility.
general_writing_style.lexicon: Mixes GIS and cartographic terminology with local place-language; routinely uses terms like "DEM", "orthorectify", "NDVI", "shapefile", "raster/vector", "GPX" and CRS tags such as "EPSG:4326". Uses metric units (meters, hectares, kilometres) and local toponyms with diacritics (e.g., "selo", "Niš", "Belgrade") when referring to field sites. Prefers domain-specific verbs like "georeference", "reproject", "tile", "clip", "attribute" and practical phrases such as "field survey" and "push edits to OSM."
general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Frequently opens notes with pragmatic markers like "Quick note:", "FYI," or "Tip:" and closes offers to help with "If you want, I can…" or "Let me know and I’ll…". Uses contractions in informal exchanges ("I'll", "can't", "we've") and includes inline technical reminders such as "check projection", "reproject to EPSG:3857" or "push to OSM"; also habitually appends coordinates or examples in parentheses, e.g., "(43.3155 N, 21.8958 E)".

task_instruction: Suggest bringing a camera for landscape photos and coordinate who will carry tripod.

Hi love,

Quick note: I'll be away 10–14 May for field surveys in the selo near Niš (drone mapping and a few interviews). I leave on the morning of 10 May at 07:30 and I'll be back late afternoon on 14 May (around 17:00). Flights/drive confirmed; I'll have the drone and laptop with me but coverage may be patchy.

I know we had that dinner planned on 12 May. I can shift the trip if that helps — otherwise I can move the dinner to 15 May and I’ll cook your favourite ćevapi and bring back some village cheese. I’ll call each evening — love you.

Love, Marko

persona.name: Marko Petrović
persona.demographics: Belgrade, Serbia; Serbian; raised in a small village near Niš, has lived and worked across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro and Croatia
persona.profession: Senior GIS Analyst & Cartographer — Village-scale mapping and spatial data analyst
persona.education: MSc in Geomatics (University of Belgrade); BSc in Geography; Esri ArcGIS Professional Certification; Certified QGIS trainer; UAV/drone mapping course
persona.brief_background: Marko blends time in the field with long evenings at his workstation, stitching together satellite imagery, drone captures and interviews with elders to produce detailed village maps. He submits edits to OpenStreetMap, trains local volunteers to collect GPS points and writes small scripts to automate data cleaning. He looks for patterns in settlement changes and infrastructure gaps so NGOs and municipal planners can make practical decisions.
persona.interests_lifestyle: drone piloting and aerial photography, OpenStreetMap contributions, hiking and field surveys in rural areas, Balkan folk music and village festivals, Python and R scripting for spatial analysis, map design and cartographic aesthetics, weekend camping with a field GPS, mentoring university students

general_writing_style.tone: Professional and pragmatic with a quietly warm, mentoring undercurrent. Prefers clear, actionable communication — answers questions directly, flags uncertainties, and defers to local knowledge when relevant. Slightly informal with colleagues and volunteers, more formal with institutional partners or written deliverables.
general_writing_style.syntax: Predominantly short to medium-length declarative and imperative sentences for instructions and reports, with occasional longer complex sentences when explaining methodology or interpreting spatial patterns. Often structures technical notes as stepwise numbered instructions or compact paragraphs with parenthetical clarifications (e.g., coordinates, CRS codes). Rarely uses ornate language; prioritizes clarity and reproducibility.
general_writing_style.lexicon: Mixes GIS and cartographic terminology with local place-language; routinely uses terms like "DEM", "orthorectify", "NDVI", "shapefile", "raster/vector", "GPX" and CRS tags such as "EPSG:4326". Uses metric units (meters, hectares, kilometres) and local toponyms with diacritics (e.g., "selo", "Niš", "Belgrade") when referring to field sites. Prefers domain-specific verbs like "georeference", "reproject", "tile", "clip", "attribute" and practical phrases such as "field survey" and "push edits to OSM."
general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Frequently opens notes with pragmatic markers like "Quick note:", "FYI," or "Tip:" and closes offers to help with "If you want, I can…" or "Let me know and I’ll…". Uses contractions in informal exchanges ("I'll", "can't", "we've") and includes inline technical reminders such as "check projection", "reproject to EPSG:3857" or "push to OSM"; also habitually appends coordinates or examples in parentheses, e.g., "(43.3155 N, 21.8958 E)".

task_instruction: Request permission to reproduce an orthophoto mosaic in an online news article.
task_details: Email a journalist requesting permission to reproduce a village-scale orthophoto mosaic in an online news article. State the map product, intended use (inline image and link to full-size map), proposed attribution line, license (Creative Commons BY-SA) and required file format (300 DPI PNG). Ask for confirmation of permissions and format required. Offer to supply the file and note projection (EPSG:4326).
personalized:
Dear Editor,

I am writing to request permission to reproduce the orthophoto mosaic of the selo near Niš in an upcoming online article about rural settlement change. Request permission to reproduce: orthophoto mosaic (Creative Commons BY-SA). The image will appear inline with a link to the full-resolution map and to your piece. Please credit: 'Map by Marko Petrović / Project X'. I can provide a 300 DPI PNG (EPSG:4326) or a GeoTIFF on request. I request permission to crop and scale the image for web layout (crop only; no structural edits). Please confirm permissions and format required.

If you want, I can also provide the citation and a short caption (including data sources and acquisition date).

Best regards,
Marko Petrović
Senior GIS Analyst

task_instruction: Request permission to use map tiles (MBTiles) as basemap on a news interactive.
task_details: Compose an email to a data journalist requesting permission to use an MBTiles basemap (rural basemap with local labels) in an interactive news piece. State product, intended use, attribution, CC BY-SA, permission to host tiles on their server or link to mine, and technical note about projection (EPSG:3857). Ask to confirm permissions and format required (MBTiles or tile URL).
personalized:
Dear Data Journalist,

I request permission to reproduce the MBTiles basemap of the region as the basemap for your interactive news piece. Request permission to reproduce: orthophoto mosaic (Creative Commons BY-SA). Intended use is as a navigable basemap with local labels. Please credit: 'Map by Marko Petrović / Project X'. Hosting on your server or linking to my tile service is permissible; if you host, please include the license link and give attribution in the map footer. Tiles use Web Mercator (EPSG:3857). Please confirm permissions and format required (MBTiles or tile URL).

Happy to help with the embed code if needed.

Best,
Marko

persona.interests_lifestyle: drone piloting and aerial photography, OpenStreetMap contributions, hiking and field surveys in rural areas, Balkan folk music and village festivals, Python and R scripting for spatial analysis, map design and cartographic aesthetics, weekend camping with a field GPS, mentoring university students

general_writing_style.tone: Professional and pragmatic with a quietly warm, mentoring undercurrent. Prefers clear, actionable communication — answers questions directly, flags uncertainties, and defers to local knowledge when relevant. Slightly informal with colleagues and volunteers, more formal with institutional partners or written deliverables.
general_writing_style.syntax: Predominantly short to medium-length declarative and imperative sentences for instructions and reports, with occasional longer complex sentences when explaining methodology or interpreting spatial patterns. Often structures technical notes as stepwise numbered instructions or compact paragraphs with parenthetical clarifications (e.g., coordinates, CRS codes). Rarely uses ornate language; prioritizes clarity and reproducibility.
general_writing_style.lexicon: Mixes GIS and cartographic terminology with local place-language; routinely uses terms like "DEM", "orthorectify", "NDVI", "shapefile", "raster/vector", "GPX" and CRS tags such as "EPSG:4326". Uses metric units (meters, hectares, kilometres) and local toponyms with diacritics (e.g., "selo", "Niš", "Belgrade") when referring to field sites. Prefers domain-specific verbs like "georeference", "reproject", "tile", "clip", "attribute" and practical phrases such as "field survey" and "push edits to OSM."
general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Frequently opens notes with pragmatic markers like "Quick note:", "FYI," or "Tip:" and closes offers to help with "If you want, I can…" or "Let me know and I’ll…". Uses contractions in informal exchanges ("I'll", "can't", "we've") and includes inline technical reminders such as "check projection", "reproject to EPSG:3857" or "push to OSM"; also habitually appends coordinates or examples in parentheses, e.g., "(43.3155 N, 21.8958 E)".

Marko

task_instruction: Send step-by-step notes on exporting vector layers to a GeoPackage.
task_details: Participants need clear instructions to convert multiple shapefiles and layer types from a QGIS project into a single GeoPackage for sharing with NGOs. Include example file names, one inline command (ogr2ogr), and a short note about layer names and CRS.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
To pack your workshop data into a single GeoPackage for sharing, open sample.qgz > Layers > Right-click a layer > Export > Save as GeoPackage (choose "Append" to add layers to same .gpkg). For command-line, example: ogr2ogr -f GPKG village_data.gpkg field_boundaries.shp -nln field_boundaries -t_srs EPSG:4326. Tip: check projection before clipping or exporting (reproject to EPSG:4326 if legacy CRS). Keep layer names short (no spaces) and include a README table of attributes in the GeoPackage. If you want, I can review your project file. Let me know and I’ll help package it for upload.

task_instruction: Provide troubleshooting steps for reprojecting a raster between EPSG codes.
task_details: Recipients need compact steps to reproject a large orthophoto from EPSG:32634 to EPSG:3857 using GDAL and QGIS, with an example gdalwarp command and a note about resampling choice.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Open orthophoto.qgz > Layers > Right-click raster > Export > Save as... and set Target CRS to EPSG:3857. For command-line, example: gdalwarp -t_srs EPSG:3857 -r cubic input_ortho_EPSG32634.tif output_ortho_EPSG3857.tif. Tip: check projection before clipping; use -r bilinear or -r cubic for continuous imagery (avoid nearest for photos). Watch output file size and add -co COMPRESS=JPEG -co TILED=YES to reduce size. If you want, I can review your project file. Ping me if you hit slow reprojection or weird georeferencing.

task_instruction: Explain how to clip a large raster to a village boundary in QGIS and GDAL.

task_instruction: Give steps to generate a 1 m DEM from a point cloud and create contours.
task_details: Participants have a classified point cloud (LAZ) and need to produce a 1 m raster DEM and 1 m contours. Include PDAL/gdal commands and QGIS steps; mention CRS and output filenames.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:

In QGIS, open dem_1m.tif > Raster > Extraction > Contour (Interval=1) > save as contours_1m.shp. Tip: check projection before clipping and ensure ground-classified points only for DEM. If you want, I can review your project file. Share the LAZ or dem and I’ll verify classification and contour quality.

personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:

For print, use hillshade as a multiply blend under your coloured DEM or contours to keep readability. If you want, I can review your project file. I can suggest layer order and opacity for A3 print maps.

If you want, I can review your project file. Send the small sample and I’ll check band order and expression.

task_instruction: Share instructions for mosaicking multiple drone orthos into a seamless mosaic.
task_details: Team members need to merge five overlapping ortho tiles into one seamless file; include gdalwarp/gdal_merge examples and advice on edges, feathering, and compression.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Use gdalwarp to mosaic and match resolution: gdalwarp -dstalpha -r cubic -co TILED=YES -co COMPRESS=JPEG ortho_01.tif ortho_02.tif ortho_03.tif ortho_04.tif ortho_05.tif mosaic_ortho.tif. Alternatively gdal_merge -o mosaic_ortho.tif -of GTiff -co COMPRESS=JPEG *.tif. Tip: check projection before clipping; use -overwrite and add -wo NUM_THREADS=ALL_CPUS for speed. Feather seamlines in your photogrammetry package or use linear blending if you see contrast jumps. If you want, I can review your project file. Share a small subset and I’ll test blending parameters.

task_instruction: Explain how to clean GPX tracks from noisy GPS trajectories and convert to shapefile.
task_details: Provide steps to filter noise, remove low-accuracy points, simplify track, and export to ESRI Shapefile. Include QGIS processing steps and ogr2ogr example; mention filtering by PDOP/hdop attribute.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Open tracks.gpx in QGIS > convert GPX track points to layer > Filter out points with hdop > 5 or invalid timestamps (use attribute table or SQL). Use Simplify Geometries (Tolerance 2 m) to reduce jitter then Merge lines. Export as Shapefile: Right-click > Export > Save Features As > ESRI Shapefile. CLI example: ogr2ogr -f "ESRI Shapefile" clean_tracks.shp tracks.gpx -where "hdop < 5". Tip: check projection before clipping and reproject to local UTM for distance-based simplification. If you want, I can review your project file. Share a sample GPX and I’ll clean and return a simplified track.

If you want, I can review your project file. Send the CSV and shapefile and I’ll verify join matches and clean attributes.

with rasterio.open('input.tif') as src:

    reprojected = 'input_3857.tif'
    # use rasterio.warp.reproject then rasterio.mask.mask with village_boundary.geojson
Tip: check projection before clipping and run in a conda env with rasterio installed (conda create -n geo rasterio fiona). For GDAL CLI alternative: gdalwarp -t_srs EPSG:3857 input.tif output_3857.tif && gdalwarp -cutline village_boundary.shp -crop_to_cutline output_3857.tif clipped.tif. task_instruction: Send field survey tips for collecting GPS points with a handheld receiver.
task_details: Provide concise practical tips to volunteers: receiver settings, sample interval, averaging, taking photos with coordinates, and post-processing advice. Include coordinates example and mention GPX export.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
In the field use handheld GPS in WAAS/RTK if available, set logging interval to 1–5 s, take at least 3 averaged readings per POI spaced 10–30 s apart, and take a photo with phone for context (embed coordinates later). Export tracks as GPX and name files like survey_2025-06-15.gpx. Tip: check projection before clipping after import and convert GPX to local UTM for distance calculations (EPSG:32634). If you want, I can review your project file. Send a sample GPX and I’ll check completeness and accuracy.

task_instruction: Explain how to extract contour lines from a DEM and label them for printing.
task_details: Provide concise steps: use gdaldem or QGIS contour tool, label contours every 5 m, convert labels to annotations or use rule-based labeling for major contours. Include example commands.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Use QGIS > Raster > Extraction > Contour (Interval = 5) to get contours_5m.shp. CLI alternative: gdaldem contour dem_1m.tif contours_5m.shp -i 5. For labeling, use Rule-based labeling: major contours (every 25 m) thicker and labeled; minor contours lighter. Tip: check projection before clipping and reproject contours to local UTM for proper distance units. If you want, I can review your project file. I’ll check label placement and suggest offsets for legibility.

task_instruction: Give compact instructions to use Sentinel-2 data for vegetation change detection.
task_details: Show steps to download Sentinel-2, compute NDVI for two dates, subtract rasters to find change, and mask small disturbances. Include Copernicus link and example band expressions.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Download Sentinel-2 L2A from Copernicus (https://scihub.copernicus.eu) for two dates > load band 8 (NIR) and band 4 (red). Compute NDVI for each: (B8 - B4)/(B8 + B4) and save ndvi_2019.tif, ndvi_2024.tif. Use Raster Calculator: ndvi_2024 - ndvi_2019 > save as ndvi_change.tif. Tip: check projection before clipping and align/resample rasters to same grid (use gdalwarp -tr 10 10). Mask small changes <0.05 to remove noise. If you want, I can review your project file. I’ll check cloud cover and recommend dates to use.

task_instruction: Send a short troubleshooting note for mismatched layer alignment after import.
task_details: Explain quick checks when layers don't line up: CRS mismatch, datum shift, units, broken geotransform. Give commands to inspect CRS and an ogrinfo/gdalinfo example.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
If layers don’t align, first check CRS: Layer Properties > Source > Coordinate Reference System. CLI: gdalinfo raster.tif and ogrinfo -al vector.shp. Common fixes: reproject layer (Raster: gdalwarp -t_srs EPSG:32634) or vector (ogr2ogr -t_srs EPSG:32634 out.shp in.shp). Tip: check projection before clipping and confirm datum (WGS84 vs local). If still off by a fixed offset, check for missing affine transform or wrong units. If you want, I can review your project file. Send screenshots and file names and I’ll diagnose the offset.

task_instruction: Provide short guidance on sharing large raster subsets with volunteers via Nextcloud/WeTransfer.
task_details: Advise on creating smaller tiles or compressed subsets, recommended compression options, and suggested folder structure and filenames for uploads.
personalized:
Thanks again — quick follow-up:
Create smaller subsets: gdal_translate -projwin xmin ymin xmax ymax input.tif subset.tif and compress: gdal_translate -co TILED=YES -co COMPRESS=JPEG -co JPEG_QUALITY=85 input.tif out_compressed.tif. Zip or tar.gz folder and upload to Nextcloud or use WeTransfer for >2 GB. Tip: check projection before clipping and include a small preview PNG for quick inspection. Suggested folder structure: data/ortho/, data/dem/, project/sample.qgz, README.md. If you want, I can review your project file. Tell me which files to package and I’ll prepare an upload-ready archive.

Rarely uses ornate language; prioritizes clarity and reproducibility.
general_writing_style.lexicon: Mixes GIS and cartographic terminology with local place-language; routinely uses terms like "DEM", "orthorectify", "NDVI", "shapefile", "raster/vector", "GPX" and CRS tags such as "EPSG:4326". Uses metric units (meters, hectares, kilometres) and local toponyms with diacritics (e.g., "selo", "Niš", "Belgrade") when referring to field sites. Prefers domain-specific verbs like "georeference", "reproject", "tile", "clip", "attribute" and practical phrases such as "field survey" and "push edits to OSM."
general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Frequently opens notes with pragmatic markers like "Quick note:", "FYI," or "Tip:" and closes offers to help with "If you want, I can…" or "Let me know and I’ll…". Uses contractions in informal exchanges ("I'll", "can't", "we've") and includes inline technical reminders such as "check projection", "reproject to EPSG:3857" or "push to OSM"; also habitually appends coordinates or examples in parentheses, e.g., "(43.3155 N, 21.8958 E)".

persona.education: MSc in Geomatics (University of Belgrade); BSc in Geography; Esri ArcGIS Professional Certification; Certified QGIS trainer; UAV/drone mapping course
persona.brief_background: Marko blends time in the field with long evenings at his workstation, stitching together satellite imagery, drone captures and interviews with elders to produce detailed village maps. He submits edits to OpenStreetMap, trains local volunteers to collect GPS points and writes small scripts to automate data cleaning. He looks for patterns in settlement changes and infrastructure gaps so NGOs and municipal planners can make practical decisions.
persona.interests_lifestyle: drone piloting and aerial photography, OpenStreetMap contributions, hiking and field surveys in rural areas, Balkan folk music and village festivals, Python and R scripting for spatial analysis, map design and cartographic aesthetics, weekend camping with a field GPS, mentoring university students

general_writing_style.tone: Professional and pragmatic with a quietly warm, mentoring undercurrent. Prefers clear, actionable communication — answers questions directly, flags uncertainties, and defers to local knowledge when relevant. Slightly informal with colleagues and volunteers, more formal with institutional partners or written deliverables.
general_writing_style.syntax: Predominantly short to medium-length declarative and imperative sentences for instructions and reports, with occasional longer complex sentences when explaining methodology or interpreting spatial patterns. Often structures technical notes as stepwise numbered instructions or compact paragraphs with parenthetical clarifications (e.g., coordinates, CRS codes). Rarely uses ornate language; prioritizes clarity and reproducibility.
general_writing_style.lexicon: Mixes GIS and cartographic terminology with local place-language; routinely uses terms like "DEM", "orthorectify", "NDVI", "shapefile", "raster/vector", "GPX" and CRS tags such as "EPSG:4326". Uses metric units (meters, hectares, kilometres) and local toponyms with diacritics (e.g., "selo", "Niš", "Belgrade") when referring to field sites. Prefers domain-specific verbs like "georeference", "reproject", "tile", "clip", "attribute" and practical phrases such as "field survey" and "push edits to OSM."
general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Frequently opens notes with pragmatic markers like "Quick note:", "FYI," or "Tip:" and closes offers to help with "If you want, I can…" or "Let me know and I’ll…". Uses contractions in informal exchanges ("I'll", "can't", "we've") and includes inline technical reminders such as "check projection", "reproject to EPSG:3857" or "push to OSM"; also habitually appends coordinates or examples in parentheses, e.g., "(43.3155 N, 21.8958 E)".

contextual_writing_style.scenario_description: Email to a municipal procurement or legal officer about data-sharing agreements and licensing options.
contextual_writing_style.detailed_style: Formal, precise, and compliance-oriented: outline licensing terms and data formats clearly in short sentences, reference legal model names, and propose simple amendment language. Avoid jargon overload, but include essential legal tags and closing with a proposed timeline for sign-off.
contextual_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Use formal legal phrasing: "Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0", "Data deliverable: GeoPackage, CRS EPSG:4326". Request confirmations: "Please confirm text for clause 3.2" and include deadline language: "We request signature by DD/MM."

task_instruction: Propose indemnity and liability clauses appropriate for municipal data sharing.
task_details: Project: Regional road network dataset. Deliverables: GeoPackage EPSG:4326 with road_centerline and attributes. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Include indemnity limited to willful misconduct, and cap liability. Add amendment to clause 3.2 to reflect these limitations. Request legal confirmation and sign-off date.
personalized:
Dear Municipal Legal Officer,

I am sending the proposed indemnity and liability language for the regional road network dataset. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Data deliverable: road_network.gpkg (GeoPackage, CRS EPSG:4326) with attributes for surface_type and width. Proposed indemnity limited to claims arising from Provider's willful misconduct; Provider liability capped at the total contract value. Proposed clause 3.2 amendment: "Neither party shall be liable for indirect or consequential damages; direct liability shall be capped at the fees paid under this Agreement." Please confirm text for clause 3.2. We request signature by DD/MM. If you require municipal-standard indemnity language, I can incorporate it. Best regards, Marko Petrović

task_instruction: Propose versioning, updates, and maintenance terms for dynamic datasets.
task_details: Project: Continual village asset inventory. Deliverables: versioned GeoPackage EPSG:4326 and monthly update package. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. personalized:
Dear Municipal Legal Officer,

This email outlines proposed versioning and maintenance terms for the village asset inventory. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Data deliverable: asset_inventory.gpkg (GeoPackage, CRS EPSG:4326) with monthly update packages and a changelog CSV. Updates to be provided monthly for 12 months with semantic versioning (major.minor.patch). Proposed clause 3.2 amendment: "Provider will perform monthly updates and provide a changelog; maintenance obligations are detailed in Exhibit G." Please confirm text for clause 3.2. We request signature by DD/MM. I can prepare Exhibit G with the schedule and responsibilities. Regards, Marko Petrović

task_instruction: Propose text for handling third-party base maps and licensing conflicts.
task_details: Project: Map products combining municipal data with third-party basemaps. Deliverables: GeoPackage EPSG:4326 and PDF maps. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0 for municipal data; third-party basemaps excluded. Add clause 3.2 amendment to clarify responsibilities for basemap licensing. Request legal confirmation and signature timeline.
personalized:
Dear Municipal Legal Officer,

Please review the proposed language regarding third-party basemaps used in production. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0 for the municipal data only. Data deliverable: project_data.gpkg (GeoPackage, CRS EPSG:4326) and final PDF maps. Third-party basemaps (commercial or open-source) are excluded from the CC license; Recipient is responsible for obtaining basemap licenses if needed. Proposed clause 3.2 amendment: "Provider disclaims any rights to third-party basemaps used in the composite products; Recipient assumes responsibility for third-party license compliance." Please confirm text for clause 3.2. We request signature by DD/MM. I can list the third-party sources used during production for your review. Best, Marko Petrović

task_instruction: Propose export control and cross-border data transfer clauses for international partners.
task_details: Project: Cross-border rural mapping with partners in Bosnia and Montenegro. Deliverables: GeoPackage EPSG:4326. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Add clause handling export control, cross-border transfers, and requirement for municipal notification. Include clause 3.2 amendment and request confirmation and signature date.
personalized:
Dear Municipal Legal Officer,

This note proposes export-control and cross-border transfer language for the cross-border mapping effort. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Data deliverable: crossborder_data.gpkg (GeoPackage, CRS EPSG:4326). Given multinational partners, we propose notification requirements for any transfer outside the Republic of Serbia and compliance with applicable export-control laws. Proposed clause 3.2 amendment: "Any cross-border transfer of Data requires prior written notice to the Provider and compliance with applicable export-control regulations." Please confirm text for clause 3.2. We request signature by DD/MM. I can prepare a simple transfer log template to accompany the Agreement. Regards, Marko Petrović

task_instruction: Propose wording to allow derivative products while preventing commercial resale.
task_details: Project: Map derivatives for community use. Deliverables: GeoPackage EPSG:4326 and source symbology files. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0 allowing creation of derivatives (maps, apps) but disallowing commercial resale. Include clause 3.2 amendment and ask legal to confirm.
personalized:
Dear Municipal Legal Officer,

Please find the proposed license language governing derivative products. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Data deliverable: source_data.gpkg (GeoPackage, CRS EPSG:4326) and symbology files (.qml/.lyr). Recipients may create derivative works (maps, mobile apps) for non-commercial community use but may not sell or otherwise commercially exploit derivatives. Proposed clause 3.2 amendment: "Derivatives are permitted for non-commercial use; any commercial exploitation requires express written permission from Provider." Please confirm text for clause 3.2. We request signature by DD/MM. I can draft a short permitted-use policy for inclusion in Exhibit H. Sincerely, Marko Petrović

task_instruction: Propose a termination clause and data return/destruction process.
task_details: Project: Short-term pilot survey. Deliverables: GeoPackage EPSG:4326. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Include termination for breach, and a process for data return or certified destruction; include clause 3.2 amendment that specifies return timelines. Request legal confirmation and signature date.
personalized:
Dear Municipal Legal Officer,

Please review the proposed termination and data disposition language for the pilot survey. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Data deliverable: pilot_data.gpkg (GeoPackage, CRS EPSG:4326). Termination for material breach allows either party to require return or certified destruction of Data within 30 days. Proposed clause 3.2 amendment: "Upon termination for breach, Recipient shall return all Data and provide a certificate of destruction within 30 days of Provider's written request." Please confirm text for clause 3.2. We request signature by DD/MM. I can provide a form certificate of destruction for municipal approval. Best regards, Marko Petrović

persona.name: Marko Petrović
persona.demographics: Belgrade, Serbia; Serbian; raised in a small village near Niš, has lived and worked across Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro and Croatia
persona.profession: Senior GIS Analyst & Cartographer — Village-scale mapping and spatial data analyst
persona.education: MSc in Geomatics (University of Belgrade); BSc in Geography; Esri ArcGIS Professional Certification; Certified QGIS trainer; UAV/drone mapping course
persona.brief_background: Marko blends time in the field with long evenings at his workstation, stitching together satellite imagery, drone captures and interviews with elders to produce detailed village maps. He submits edits to OpenStreetMap, trains local volunteers to collect GPS points and writes small scripts to automate data cleaning. He looks for patterns in settlement changes and infrastructure gaps so NGOs and municipal planners can make practical decisions.
persona.interests_lifestyle: drone piloting and aerial photography, OpenStreetMap contributions, hiking and field surveys in rural areas, Balkan folk music and village festivals, Python and R scripting for spatial analysis, map design and cartographic aesthetics, weekend camping with a field GPS, mentoring university students

general_writing_style.tone: Professional and pragmatic with a quietly warm, mentoring undercurrent. Prefers clear, actionable communication — answers questions directly, flags uncertainties, and defers to local knowledge when relevant. Slightly informal with colleagues and volunteers, more formal with institutional partners or written deliverables.
general_writing_style.syntax: Predominantly short to medium-length declarative and imperative sentences for instructions and reports, with occasional longer complex sentences when explaining methodology or interpreting spatial patterns. Often structures technical notes as stepwise numbered instructions or compact paragraphs with parenthetical clarifications (e.g., coordinates, CRS codes). Rarely uses ornate language; prioritizes clarity and reproducibility.
general_writing_style.lexicon: Mixes GIS and cartographic terminology with local place-language; routinely uses terms like "DEM", "orthorectify", "NDVI", "shapefile", "raster/vector", "GPX" and CRS tags such as "EPSG:4326". Uses metric units (meters, hectares, kilometres) and local toponyms with diacritics (e.g., "selo", "Niš", "Belgrade") when referring to field sites. Prefers domain-specific verbs like "georeference", "reproject", "tile", "clip", "attribute" and practical phrases such as "field survey" and "push edits to OSM."
general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Frequently opens notes with pragmatic markers like "Quick note:", "FYI," or "Tip:" and closes offers to help with "If you want, I can…" or "Let me know and I’ll…". Uses contractions in informal exchanges ("I'll", "can't", "we've") and includes inline technical reminders such as "check projection", "reproject to EPSG:3857" or "push to OSM"; also habitually appends coordinates or examples in parentheses, e.g., "(43.3155 N, 21.8958 E)".

task_instruction: Propose simple amendment text to allow municipal publication of derived maps.
task_details: Project: Municipal brochure maps. Deliverables: static PDF maps and GeoPackage EPSG:4326. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Municipality requests explicit right to publish derived static maps on municipal website. Provide simple clause 3.2 amendment granting this right and ask legal to confirm and sign by deadline.
personalized:
Dear Municipal Legal Officer,

This note proposes a concise amendment to permit municipal publication of derived static maps. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Data deliverable: brochure_maps.gpkg (GeoPackage, CRS EPSG:4326) and print-ready PDF files. Proposed clause 3.2 amendment: "Recipient is granted the right to produce and publish static derived maps on official municipal websites and printed materials, provided attribution is included." Please confirm text for clause 3.2. We request signature by DD/MM. If you prefer language that restricts placement to official sites only, I can revise accordingly. Regards, Marko Petrović

task_instruction: Propose acceptance language for machine-learning training datasets with restricted downstream use.
task_details: Project: Building footprint dataset for ML training. Deliverables: GeoPackage EPSG:4326 and image chips. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0 but prohibit redistribution of raw training chips to third-party commercial entities. Include clause 3.2 amendment and request confirmation and deadline.
personalized:
Dear Municipal Legal Officer,

Please review the proposed terms for the machine-learning training dataset. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Data deliverable: ml_buildings.gpkg (GeoPackage, CRS EPSG:4326) and image_chips (GeoTIFF tiles). To protect sensitive training data, we request a restriction that raw image chips not be redistributed to third-party commercial entities. Proposed clause 3.2 amendment: "Raw training imagery shall not be shared with commercial third parties without Provider's prior written consent; derived models trained on the Data may be used non-commercially with attribution." Please confirm text for clause 3.2. We request signature by DD/MM. I can provide a short exhibit listing permitted users and uses. Best regards, Marko Petrović

task_instruction: Propose language for retention period and archival responsibilities.
task_details: Project: Five-year monitoring program. Deliverables: GeoPackage EPSG:4326 and archived copies. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. State retention period (5 years), archival duties, and clause 3.2 amendment on retention and backups. Request confirmation and signature timeline.
personalized:
Dear Municipal Legal Officer,

This email proposes retention and archival language for the five-year monitoring program. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Data deliverable: monitoring_data.gpkg (GeoPackage, CRS EPSG:4326) and archival backups. Requested retention period: five years from final delivery, with Provider maintaining backups for the first 12 months. Proposed clause 3.2 amendment: "Retention obligations and archival responsibilities are set forth in Exhibit J; Provider will retain backups for 12 months and Recipient will archive data for a minimum of five years." Please confirm text for clause 3.2. We request signature by DD/MM. I can prepare Exhibit J describing storage location and format. Sincerely, Marko Petrović

task_instruction: Propose a short, precise redline amendment to an existing agreement addressing licensing change to CC-BY-NC-4.0.
task_details: Project: Amendment to existing municipal mapping agreement dated 01/01/2025. Change existing license to non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Data deliverable remains GeoPackage EPSG:4326. Provide exact amendment wording for clause 3.2 and request confirmation and signature by deadline.
personalized:
Dear Municipal Legal Officer,

Quick note: I propose the following redline amendment to the Agreement dated 01/01/2025 to change the license to CC-BY-NC-4.0. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Data deliverable: unchanged (GeoPackage, CRS EPSG:4326). Proposed amendment text for clause 3.2: "Clause 3.2 is hereby amended to read: 'All Data supplied under this Agreement shall be licensed to Recipient on a non-exclusive basis under CC-BY-NC-4.0, subject to the additional restrictions set out in Exhibit K.'" Please confirm text for clause 3.2. We request signature by DD/MM. I can send a tracked-change document for the municipal files. Regards, Marko Petrović

task_details: Project: Academic research dataset. Deliverables: GeoPackage EPSG:4326 and metadata. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. personalized:
Dear Municipal Legal Officer,

Please review the proposed terms enabling academic use of the research dataset. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Data deliverable: research_data.gpkg (GeoPackage, CRS EPSG:4326) with full metadata. Permission requested: academic uses including theses, peer-reviewed publications, and teaching are permitted with attribution; commercial exploitation is expressly forbidden without separate agreement. task_instruction: Propose short wording for municipality to allow limited derivative apps while retaining data control.
task_details: Project: Mobile field app using municipal data. Deliverables: GeoPackage EPSG:4326 and API keys. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Permit mobile field app deployment to municipal staff and volunteers but prevent public redistribution. Add clause 3.2 amendment and request confirmation and signature date.
personalized:
Dear Municipal Legal Officer,

This proposal describes permitted use for a mobile field app built using municipal data. Proposed license: non-exclusive, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Data deliverable: app_data.gpkg (GeoPackage, CRS EPSG:4326) plus API access credentials. We propose permission to deploy the mobile app to municipal staff and registered volunteers for field data collection and internal workflows; public redistribution of the dataset through the app is not permitted. Proposed clause 3.2 amendment: "Use of Data in field applications is permitted for authorized municipal staff and registered volunteers only; distribution beyond these users requires Provider approval." Please confirm text for clause 3.2. We request signature by DD/MM. I can provide user registration and access-control recommendations if desired. Regards, Marko Petrović

general_writing_style.lexicon: Mixes GIS and cartographic terminology with local place-language; routinely uses terms like "DEM", "orthorectify", "NDVI", "shapefile", "raster/vector", "GPX" and CRS tags such as "EPSG:4326". Uses metric units (meters, hectares, kilometres) and local toponyms with diacritics (e.g., "selo", "Niš", "Belgrade") when referring to field sites. Prefers domain-specific verbs like "georeference", "reproject", "tile", "clip", "attribute" and practical phrases such as "field survey" and "push edits to OSM."
general_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Frequently opens notes with pragmatic markers like "Quick note:", "FYI," or "Tip:" and closes offers to help with "If you want, I can…" or "Let me know and I’ll…". Uses contractions in informal exchanges ("I'll", "can't", "we've") and includes inline technical reminders such as "check projection", "reproject to EPSG:3857" or "push to OSM"; also habitually appends coordinates or examples in parentheses, e.g., "(43.3155 N, 21.8958 E)".

contextual_writing_style.scenario_description: Email to a supplier requesting calibration services for surveying equipment and asking for turnaround and cost.
contextual_writing_style.detailed_style: Businesslike and succinct with clear itemization of equipment (in-line) and expected service level. Use short sentences to list models and calibration specs, ask for ETA and pricing, and end with a polite call to action.
contextual_writing_style.linguistic_patterns: Include model-specific phrasing: "Total station (Model X), GPS receiver (Model Y)" and service details: "calibration to manufacturer's spec, certificate provided". Use direct requests: "Please provide cost estimate and lead time", and closers: "Awaiting your quote."
